pr_title: usb: cdc: Do not duplicate USB transfer slots for OUT transfers
pr_body:
This commit fixes an issue when more than one USB transfer is
reserved for same OUT endpoint.

There are 2 scenarios when this could happen:
- The Host sends SET_CONFIGURATION(1) request twice.
- The Host triggers Suspend->Resume->Configured
  event sequence for the device.

USB tranfers are not canceled on SUSPEND event
when the device was not configred previously.

Because of that USB transfer slot is reserved twice
for the same OUT endpoint and lead to shortage of USB
transfer slots quickly.

Without this patch CDC ACM class reserves duplicated USB
transfer slots for one transfer. The sequence of
Suspend->Resume events is genereted alongside with
Configured and the stack will shortly run out of transfer
slots.

If the Host, for some reason, decides to send
SET_CONFIGURATION request twice the same issue is seen.
This patch prevents from reserving additional USB transfer
slots twice.

Fixes #26970

issue_context.title: usb: overflow of USB transfers leads to clogging
comments:
> If USB stack is calling read transfer on every SUSPEND->RESUME it will quickly run out of transfer slots making it unable to finish the enumeration and make the device unusable.

Actually not, because SUSPEND event would cancel all transfers and cdc-acm re-triggers the transfer only for SUSPEND->RESUME transition. I need more information, logs...

> > If USB stack is calling read transfer on every SUSPEND->RESUME it will quickly run out of transfer slots making it unable to finish the enumeration and make the device unusable.
> 
> Actually not, because SUSPEND event would cancel all transfers and cdc-acm re-triggers the transfer only for SUSPEND->RESUME transition. I need more information, logs...

It seems it doesn't happen. I will post a patch that can show that. I've found that the issue could be easily addressed by this patch:

``` diff
diff --git a/subsys/usb/usb_transfer.c b/subsys/usb/usb_transfer.c
index 230337783b..f4b29f6bb7 100644
--- a/subsys/usb/usb_transfer.c
+++ b/subsys/usb/usb_transfer.c
@@ -203,6 +203,8 @@ int usb_transfer(uint8_t ep, uint8_t *data, size_t dlen, unsigned int flags,
 
 	key = irq_lock();
 
+	usb_cancel_transfer(ep);
+
 	for (i = 0; i < ARRAY_SIZE(ut_data); i++) {
 		if (!k_sem_take(&ut_data[i].sem, K_NO_WAIT)) {
 			trans = &ut_data[i];
```
I am just wondering if this should only be done for OUT endpoints.

I've added (I better like to change it to ERR instead of enabling all DBG logs) to the patch in Issue description:
``` diff
@@ -198,11 +201,13 @@ int usb_transfer(uint8_t ep, uint8_t *data, size_t dlen, unsigned int flags,
        struct usb_transfer_data *trans = NULL;
        int i, key, ret = 0;
 
-       LOG_DBG("Transfer start, ep 0x%02x, data %p, dlen %zd",
+       LOG_ERR("Transfer start, ep 0x%02x, data %p, dlen %zd",
                ep, data, dlen);
 
        key = irq_lock();
```

review_comments:
If we want to correctly detect spurious `RESUME` events then we can't do that. Imagine a situation:
`Connected->Suspend->Resume` -> The device was not yet configured and the `Resume` event is not spurious. In fact the device was suspended during the enumeration and its possible.

We could clear `dev_data->suspended = false` on each `Resume` event but then we would not trace spurious `Resume`'s. I think we can do so but I know You wanted to highlight those spurious things recently so I decided not to do so.
